- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overcorrects downward; delay or dampen the correction to allow for mean reversion.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward with more aggressive slope.
- Model tends to lag in responding to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns bullish after a downtrend; anticipate and slightly accelerate upward bias.
- In early forecast windows (e.g., 30d), model often underestimates the magnitude of later price surges; apply a mild upward bias to the tail end of the forecast.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted smoothing to favor recent sentiment direction.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history — if sentiment is volatile, don’t assume trend continuation; use sentiment as a filter, not a driver, for correction.
